description.value: Longitudinal neuropsychological and volumetric MRI study of frontotemporal dementia associated with C9ORF72 expansions, examining cognitive progression and rates and regional patterns of brain volume change.

spans.text: Here we present longitudinal neuropsychological and neuroimaging data on a cohort of patients with pathological repeat expansions in   C9ORF72  .

description.value: Retrospective longitudinal observational cohort study with repeated neuropsychological assessments and volumetric MRI scans, comparing patients with C9ORF72 expansions with healthy controls.

spans.text: The study was approved by the local research ethics committee under Declaration of Helsinki guidelines and all subjects gave informed consent for participation.
For the purpose of reporting longitudinal change only cases with a minimum of two neuropsychological assessments or volumetric MRI scans were included.

value: Mean annualised whole brain atrophy in patients with the C9ORF72 mutation was 1.4%, significantly higher than in controls (0.4%; P = 0.04). Atrophy rates varied widely between subjects, and atrophy was symmetrical between the cerebral hemispheres.
Mean brain atrophy rates were increased compared with healthy controls, although there was substantial diversity across the group.

value: Patients with a C9ORF72 mutation had a mean annualised ventricular expansion rate of 3.2 ml/year compared with 0.7 ml/year in controls (P = 0.001), with increased ventricular enlargement present in 5/6 cases.
Increased rates of ventricular expansion were consistently observed and may be a candidate biomarker of disease evolution associated with the C9ORF72 mutation.

value: Longitudinal cerebellar atrophy was present in 4/6 patients; the mean annualised rate of cerebellar atrophy was 1.0%/year in patients compared with 0.1%/year in controls (P = 0.02).
Cerebellar atrophy was a relatively prominent and consistent feature in individual cases, with an approximately 10-fold increase in mean atrophy rate compared with controls.

value: Significant subcortical volume loss over time compared with healthy controls was detected in the right thalamus (P = 0.006), left thalamus (P = 0.03) and left globus pallidus (P = 0.04).

Rates of thalamic and cerebellar atrophy and ventricular expansion were disproportionately increased relative to whole brain atrophy rates, consistent with involvement of subcortical structures and pathways.
